uplink.description: battery 3.5 V, external port 1 analog input = 3.0 V and digital input high
uplink._note: ELSYS TLV: VDD(0x07)=0x0DAC=3500 mV -> battery 3.5 V (whole-device supply rail, top level); ANALOG1(0x08)=0x0BB8=3000 mV -> port0 analog.voltage 3.0 V; EXT_DIGITAL(0x0D)=1 -> port0 action.contactState closed. Both external readings are Elsys port 1, so they are scoped into the single `port0` channels entry; port 2 reported nothing, so it gets no entry. Verified against reference/upstream-codec.js (vdd 3500, analog1 3000, digital 1).

uplink.description: external temperature-equivalent temp + relative and absolute pulse counts
uplink._note: TEMP(0x01)=0x00C8=200/10=20 degC -> air.temperature; PULSE1(0x0A)=100 -> pulse.count; PULSE1_ABS(0x0B)=0x000003E8=1000 -> pulse.total. Verified against reference/upstream-codec.js (temperature 20, pulse1 100, pulseAbs 1000).

uplink.description: payload stopping at an unsupported ELSYS type still decodes leading fields
uplink._note: ANALOG1(0x08)=0x07D0=2000 mV -> port0 analog.voltage 2.0 V, then ACC(0x03) is unsupported and stops the walk (upstream default: skip to end). A warning is emitted. Only Elsys port 1 reported, so `channels` holds a single `port0` entry.

uplink.description: both external ports populated: analog input and dry contact on each, plus the port-1-only pulse counter and probe temperature
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds ELSYS TLV frame exercising both paired external banks on BOTH ports with distinct values. Raw decode confirmed via the ORACLE method against reference/upstream-codec.js: {temperature:20, vdd:3500, analog1:3000, pulse1:100, pulseAbs:1000, externalTemperature:12.5, digital:1, analog2:3300, digital2:0}. expected.data is the authored normalization: ANALOG1/ANALOG2 -> analog.voltage in the port0/port1 entries (3.0 V / 3.3 V, mV/1000 rounded to 3), EXT_DIGITAL/EXT_DIGITAL2 -> action.contactState in the same entries (1 -> closed / 0 -> open). VDD (supply rail) -> battery, onboard TEMP -> air.temperature, and the pulse counter + probe temperature stay top-level because this decoder handles only their port-1 TLVs (0x16/0x17/0x19 are absent), leaving them without a second position to scope.
